parts.note: a Bramley is a large English cooking apple; across the Atlantic, in America, the big one is New York's nickname

explanation.surface: A question about what an English cooking apple would be called in America.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bramley is a big British cooking apple, and 'over the pond' means across the Atlantic in the USA, where the phrase is the nickname of New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of New York City is literally a phrase describing a large apple such as a Bramley.

clue.text: He's a lion, maybe, but I go on a horse

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told they may be a lion, yet they ride on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the letters of HE'S A LION. The definition speaks as the object: a small nail that fixes a shoe to a horse's hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe nail is hammered through a horseshoe into the hoof, so it literally sits on a horse.

indicators.note: heartless means losing the heart, the central letter of the word for the fugitive

parts.note: a fugitive is a runaway

explanation.surface: An escapee on the run has ended up at an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle A from RUNAWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip of an airfield where planes take off and land, standing here for the whole.

clue.text: Carbon forest settled then and there

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
Ashdown Forest is an area of heathland in East Sussex, England, home of Winnie-the-Pooh

explanation.surface: A carbon forest has become settled at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Ashdown Forest is a heath in East Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying in ready money on the spot means a bill is settled immediately, then and there.

definitions.meaning: French for 'to be idle', i.e. to loaf in French
a long thin baguette is called a stick of bread, an example of this loaf

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a joke: 'être fainéant' is French for being lazy, which is to loaf, so it is loafing in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long French loaf, also called a French stick; the French phrase means 'to be idle', i.e. to loaf.

indicators.note: in places the food word inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is a type of food

explanation.surface: A hungry person asks for something to eat in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is one who is in want, lacking the means to live and asking for help.

clue.text: Put bubbles in fresh tea — about time!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the time word is enclosed
fresh signals the letters of tea are made anew in a fresh order

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to fizz up some newly made tea, and high time too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' makes ATE from the drink, and 'about' wraps that round the period of time; 'about time!' reads as impatience but is the container plus its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate a liquid is to charge it with gas, filling it with bubbles.

clue.text: The general view is it's a vice

parts.note: greed is one of the deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: Popular opinion holds that something is a moral failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreed is what everyone accepts, the consensus or general view on a matter.

indicators.note: holds means the agent word contains the others

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
OK means approved or authorised

explanation.surface: A strange secret agent is cleared for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooky means eerie or uncanny, close in sense to weird.

clue.text: With which comic character pursues shellfish round London?

definitions.text: With which comic character pursues shellfish round London?

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so the character word follows the shellfish word

parts.note: an oyster is a shellfish
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: A funny figure chases seafood around the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is an old word for a joker or eccentric. The Oyster card is the smart ticket for travel on London's buses and Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: London's prepaid travel smartcard is the thing used for getting round the city, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Tickings off for agent and so for organiser

parts.note: a rep, a representative, acts as agent for a firm

indicators.note: an organiser arranges things, so the letters of so for are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A salesman and an event organiser both get told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproofs are rebukes or reprimands, which is what tickings off are.

parts.note: the Witch of Endor is a biblical figure, so her home is En-dor, and the 's gives a final S
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A witch's house is the central point of some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Witch of Endor appears in the First Book of Samuel; the possessive 's on 'home's' supplies an S.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to back it publicly, giving support.

clue.text: Covert plan to get little guy in drink

indicators.note: in places the little guy word inside the drink word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A secret scheme involves getting a small man into his cups.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is informal British for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch-up is a scheme arranged in secret to frame or cheat someone.

clue.text: Petted pet in quiet party held by convict

indicators.note: held by means placed within the convict word

parts.note: a lag (old lag) is a convict
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A pampered animal at a quiet gathering is grabbed by a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petted pet' sounds redundant but is precise: the definition is an animal that sits on laps to be stroked.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered pet dog, one that is stroked and fussed over.

indicators.note: about means going round the small word
playing suggests playing around with the letters of tapes

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone plays cassettes about a little bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' makes STPEA, and 'about' wraps it round the Scots word for small, which sits after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden plant grown for its scented blooms.

clue.text: Microsoft's idea to get prize of vintage port

parts.note: to win is to get a prize
Dow's is a long-established maker of vintage port

explanation.surface: Microsoft hopes to bag a prize of fine old port.
explanation.walkthrough: Microsoft's operating system is called Windows, so a single window is its idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Microsoft's operating system is named after the on-screen pane, so that pane is the firm's central concept.

clue.text: We haven't time to waste on trivia: how about art?

definitions.text: We haven't time to waste on trivia: how about art?

parts.words: We haven't time to waste on trivia: how about art?
parts.note: an excuse for skipping trivia is that our days are limited; art lasts longer, as in 'ars longa, vita brevis'

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin tag 'ars longa, vita brevis' says art is long and existence brief, hence the question about art.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when there is no time to waste on trifles, as our span is brief.

clue.text: She needn't do anything for boy to call faulty file reliable

parts.note: a lad is a boy
yo is a call or shout of greeting

indicators.note: faulty means the letters of file are wrongly ordered

parts.note: sure means dependable or reliable

explanation.surface: A woman of means has a boy report a defective file as trustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady of leisure is a woman with no need to work, so she has no obligations.

clue.text: O Swindon Town! outed from highest league — a fair cow — or a Houlier needed: would this clarion call be any compensation?

indicators.note: Houllier was a football manager; one 'needed' reorganises the side, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football fan laments Swindon Town's relegation and wonders if a new manager would console them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' signals the anagram of all the preceding letters. The line is from 'Sound, sound the clarion' by Thomas Osbert Mordaunt, often credited to Scott. Gérard Houllier managed Liverpool; Swindon Town were relegated from England's top division.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted verse opens 'Sound, sound the clarion', so this couplet is literally a clarion call to glory.

clue.text: NHS advisers are respectable and fastidious

definitions.meaning: the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence advises England's National Health Service

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the acronym of the body that advises Britain's National Health Service on treatments, and two senses of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means decent and proper, and also exact and discriminating; the acronym names England's health advisory body.
